extracted.intended_audience: researchers/practitioners in optimization and abrasive waterjet machining (readers of math.OC on arXiv)
extracted.subtask_description: A short commentary on choosing and evaluating optimization methods for estimating process parameters in abrasive waterjet machining; emphasizes correct problem formulation (predictive modelling vs. optimization of estimated-model variables) and selecting methods suited to the objective's mathematical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct problem interpretation (modeling vs optimization)
rubrics_metrics.description: "the real problem is how to build predictive models for the machining process, not to optimize the model variables using the estimate model as presented by Zain et al. (2011a)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you are solving the intended scientific task: build predictive models for the machining process rather than treating an estimated model as the direct objective for further optimization. Misinterpreting the original modelling goal can lead to inappropriate method choice and invalid conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match optimization method to objective function structure
rubrics_metrics.description: "the objective function to be optimized is an infinitely differentiable quadratic formula with box constraints, thus instead of using soft computing techniques, gradient methods that have better convergence property and are usually faster should be employed first."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the objective is smooth and quadratic with simple constraints, prefer gradient-based / classical optimization methods (which have stronger convergence guarantees and are typically faster) over stochastic soft-computing methods like GA or SA. Always examine mathematical properties (differentiability, convexity, constraint type) before selecting an optimizer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirically compare methods on solution quality and computational time
rubrics_metrics.description: "we show that the active set method outperforms GA and SA both in the machining performance and computational times (about 13 times faster than GA and 462 times faster than SA)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative comparisons of candidate methods on both objective performance (e.g., machining performance metrics) and computational efficiency (run time, iterations). Report relative speedups and performance trade-offs to justify method choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible communication when errors are identified
rubrics_metrics.description: "This commentary has been withdrawn because based on personal communication the main author of the papers commented in this commentary has understood the fundamental error he made in his papers. However, to prevent the spreading of the errors, interested readers can contact me directly to get the copy of the commentary"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If published critique or commentary would propagate an error that has since been acknowledged and corrected by the original authors, consider withdrawing or amending the public record and provide controlled access or follow-up communication to prevent misinformation. Document corrections and availability clearly.
